questions.title: Gadget Describe Method Drill
questions.description:
A robotics shop tags every gadget it stocks with a name and a price.
Write a class Gadget whose constructor stores a name and a price, plus a method describe() that returns the sentence '<name> costs <price>' with the price shown to exactly two decimal places.

Input Format:
Line 1: the gadget name (may contain spaces)
Line 2: the price (a number)

Output Format:
Print the sentence returned by describe().

Constraints:
1 <= len(name) <= 50 and 0 <= price <= 100000

questions.title: Counter Increment Method Drill
questions.description:
Drill: build a Counter class that keeps a numeric value and raises it one step at a time.
The constructor stores the starting value. The method increment() adds 1 to the stored value and returns the new value.

Input Format:
Line 1: starting value
Line 2: number of increments n

Output Format:
Call increment() n times; after each call print the returned value on its own line.

Constraints:
0 <= start <= 1000 and 1 <= n <= 100

questions.title: Box Volume Method Drill
questions.description:
Drill: a packaging app needs the volume of a rectangular box.
Write a class Box whose constructor stores length, width and height, and a method volume() that returns length * width * height.

Input Format:
One line with three space-separated integers: length width height

Output Format:
Print the value returned by volume().

Constraints:
1 <= length, width, height <= 1000

questions.title: Student Average Marks Method
questions.description:
Drill: a class register stores a student's marks in a list inside the object.
Write a class Student whose constructor stores the student's name and the list of marks, and a method average() that returns the mean of the marks.

Input Format:
Line 1: student name (may contain spaces)
Line 2: number of marks n
Line 3: n space-separated integers

Output Format:
Print '<name>: <average>' with the average rounded to exactly two decimal places.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50 and 0 <= mark <= 100

questions.title: Two Laptop Objects Printed
questions.description:
Drill: create two separate objects from the same class and show that each keeps its own attribute values.
Write a class Laptop whose constructor stores a brand and a ram size. Create two Laptop objects from two input lines and print each object's stored data.

Input Format:
Line 1: brand ram of the first laptop (space separated)
Line 2: brand ram of the second laptop (space separated)

Output Format:
Two lines, one per object in creation order: '<brand> - <ram>GB'

Constraints:
1 <= len(brand) <= 20 and 2 <= ram <= 512
questions.sourcecode:
class Laptop:
    def __init__(self, brand, ram):
        self.brand = brand
        self.ram = ram

brand1, ram1 = input().split()
brand2, ram2 = input().split()
first = Laptop(brand1, int(ram1))
second = Laptop(brand2, int(ram2))
print(f"{first.brand} - {first.ram}GB")
print(f"{second.brand} - {second.ram}GB")

questions.title: Label Uppercase Brand Method
questions.description:
Drill: a sticker printer needs brand names shouted in capitals.
Write a class Label whose constructor stores a brand string, and a method shout() that returns the brand converted to uppercase.

Input Format:
One line: the brand (may contain spaces)

Output Format:
Print the string returned by shout().

1 <= len(brand) <= 40

questions.title: Thermostat Warm Cool Verdict
questions.description:
A smart-home hub polls the living-room thermostat and must decide what the unit should do next.
Write a class Thermostat whose constructor stores the current temperature and the target temperature, and a method verdict() that returns WARMING when the current temperature is below the target, COOLING when it is above the target, and HOLDING when they are equal.

Input Format:
One line: current target (two space-separated integers)

Output Format:
Print the word returned by verdict().

Constraints:
-10 <= current, target <= 45

questions.title: Bakery Batch Cost Tracker
questions.description:
A bakery logs every batch it bakes with the item name, how many pieces were made and the price per piece.
Write a class Batch whose constructor stores the item name, the quantity and the unit price, and a method total_cost() that returns quantity * unit_price.

Input Format:
Line 1: item name (may contain spaces)
Line 2: quantity and unit price (space separated, unit price may be fractional)

Output Format:
Print 'Batch <item>: <total>' with the total to exactly two decimal places.

Constraints:
0 <= quantity <= 1000 and 0 <= unit_price <= 5000
questions.sourcecode:
class Batch:
    def __init__(self, item, quantity, unit_price):
        self.item = item
        self.quantity = quantity
        self.unit_price = unit_price

    def total_cost(self):
        return self.quantity * self.unit_price

item = input()
quantity, unit_price = input().split()
b = Batch(item, int(quantity), float(unit_price))
print(f"Batch {b.item}: {b.total_cost():.2f}")

questions.title: Gym Member Visit Tier
questions.description:
A fitness club awards a loyalty tier based on how many times a member has checked in this month: 10 or more visits is GOLD, 5 to 9 visits is SILVER, anything less is BRONZE.
Write a class Member whose constructor stores the member's name and starts the visit count at 0, a method check_in() that adds one visit, and a method tier() that returns the member's tier word.

Input Format:
Line 1: member name (may contain spaces)
Line 2: number of check-ins n

Output Format:
Call check_in() n times, then print '<name>: <visits> visits <tier>'.

Constraints:
1 <= len(name) <= 30 and 0 <= n <= 1000

questions.title: Robot Move Command Tracker
questions.description:
A floor-cleaning robot starts at a grid position and executes a list of movement commands: U (up), D (down), L (left), R (right), each followed by a number of steps.
Write a class Robot whose constructor stores the starting x and y, a method move(direction, steps) that updates the position, and a method report() that returns the final position as 'x y'.

Input Format:
Line 1: starting x and y (space separated)
Line 2: number of commands n
Next n lines: a command letter and a step count, space separated

Output Format:
Print the string returned by report() after all commands.

Constraints:
-100 <= x, y <= 100, 1 <= n <= 50, 1 <= steps <= 100 and every command letter is U, D, L or R

questions.title: Bank Account Operation Ledger
questions.description:
A bank teller terminal runs a list of operations on one account. Deposits only succeed for positive amounts; withdrawals only succeed when the amount is positive AND the balance covers it, otherwise the terminal prints Insufficient funds for that operation.
Write a class BankAccount whose constructor stores the owner and the starting balance, a method deposit(amount) that ignores non-positive amounts, and a method withdraw(amount) that returns True on success and False otherwise.

Input Format:
Line 1: owner and starting balance (space separated)
Line 2: number of operations n
Next n lines: DEPOSIT amount or WITHDRAW amount

Output Format:
For every failed withdrawal print Insufficient funds (in input order). At the end print 'Final balance: <balance>' with two decimal places.

Constraints:
owner is one word, 0 <= balance <= 100000, 1 <= n <= 20 and 0 <= amount <= 100000

questions.title: Employee Payroll Net Salary
questions.description:
A payroll clerk computes the net salary of employees from a base salary and a performance rating. Rating A earns a 20 percent bonus, rating B earns 10 percent and rating C earns 5 percent.
Write a class Employee whose constructor stores the name, the base salary and the rating, and a method net_salary() that returns base plus the rating-based bonus.

Input Format:
Line 1: number of employees n
Next n lines: name base rating (space separated, rating is A, B or C)

Output Format:
One line per employee in input order: '<name>: <net salary>' with two decimal places.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 20, 0 <= base <= 100000, rating is A, B or C and name is one word

questions.title: Two Carts Per Instance Items
questions.description:
A junior developer wrote a shopping-cart class whose item list was a class attribute, so every customer shared one giant list. Fix the design: each Cart object must create its own empty item list inside its constructor and grow it with append.

questions.title: Climate Unit Private Celsius
questions.description:
An IoT climate controller keeps its celsius reading as a private attribute so no code can touch it directly. A telemetry exporter, however, is allowed to read the raw value through the mangled attribute name _ClimateUnit__celsius.
Write a class ClimateUnit whose constructor stores the reading in a private attribute, a method adjust(delta) that shifts the reading, and a method fahrenheit() that returns celsius * 9 / 5 + 32.

Input Format:
Line 1: initial celsius reading (may be fractional)
Line 2: number of adjustments n
Next n lines: one delta value each (may be negative or fractional)

Output Format:
Line 1: 'Fahrenheit: <value>' with two decimal places.
Line 2: 'Internal celsius: <value>' read through the mangled name _ClimateUnit__celsius, with two decimal places.

-50 <= celsius <= 150, 0 <= n <= 20 and -20 <= delta <= 20

A perishable item is worth quantity * unit_price discounted by 10 percent (multiply by 0.9) because of spoilage risk. questions.title: Hall Seat Counter Assignment
questions.description:
An exam control room assigns hall seat numbers from one class-level counter, so every seat created anywhere shares a single sequence starting at 1. The hall has a capacity; applicants who arrive after the hall is full are rejected.
Write a class ExamSeat with a class attribute next_number set to 1. Its constructor stores the student name, takes the current counter value as the seat number, and then advances the shared counter by 1. Write a class Hall whose constructor stores the capacity and an empty seat list; its method seat(student) creates an ExamSeat while the hall is below capacity and returns '<student>: seat <number>', otherwise returns '<student>: HALL FULL'.

Input Format:
Line 1: capacity and number of applicants n (space separated)
Next n lines: one student name each

Output Format:
One line per applicant in arrival order.
Then 'Assigned: <count>' and 'Next seat: <ExamSeat.next_number>'.

Constraints:
1 <= capacity <= 100, 1 <= n <= 200 and 1 <= len(name) <= 20

questions.sourcecode:
class ExamSeat:
    next_number = 1

    def __init__(self, student):
        self.student = student
        self.seat_no = ExamSeat.next_number
        ExamSeat.next_number += 1

class Hall:
    def __init__(self, capacity):
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.seats = []

    def seat(self, student):
        if len(self.seats) < self.capacity:
            s = ExamSeat(student)
            self.seats.append(s)
            return f"{student}: seat {s.seat_no}"
        return f"{student}: HALL FULL"

capacity, n = input().split()
hall = Hall(int(capacity))
n = int(n)
for _ in range(n):
    name = input()
    print(hall.seat(name))
print(f"Assigned: {len(hall.seats)}")
print(f"Next seat: {ExamSeat.next_number}")
